resources.string: Number row
Show a row of digits above the letters

The keyboard adds a row of digits from 1 to 0 above the letter keys, so you do not press and hold for a digit. The digits on the press and hold of the top letter row are not available while this is on. The keyboard becomes one row taller.
Number row height
The height of the digit row, separate from the letter keys
A short digit row keeps fast access to the numbers. It adds less height to the keyboard than a full row.
Hints on the number row
The small symbols in the corners of the digit keys. Off hides them on that row only
Symbols on shift
Press and hold shift to change the digit row to symbols

While you hold shift on the letter layout, the number row shows the fill row of the symbol layer (= \\ < > [ ] { } | ~) instead of the digits. You reach those symbols with one shift, and you do not change to the symbols layer. On the second symbols layer, the number row already shows more arrow and comparison symbols.
Number row in symbols
Keep the digit row on the ?123 symbols layer too

The digit row stays in place when you change to the symbols layer. This is the default. Turn it off to drop the digits from the ?123 layer and keep them on the letters, where the number row is already showing them. The symbols keep their bracket and maths row, so nothing but the digits goes, and the keyboard is one row shorter on the symbols layer.
Symbol row on number pads
Keep the row above the keypad in number and phone fields

A number, phone, date or time field gets a keypad, which already leads with the digits, so the number row carries symbols instead: + * # , ; ( ) - / . on a phone field, and + - * / = ( ) % : . on the others. This is the default. Turn it off to type on the bare keypad, one row shorter. The digit row over the letters is not affected.
Arrow keys row
Show left, up, down and right keys under the keyboard

The keyboard adds a row of four arrow keys under the spacebar, so you can move the cursor without the toolbar or a drag on the spacebar. Hold an arrow to keep moving. The row is as tall as the number row, and the keyboard grows by that much.
Arrow order
Drag the handles to put the arrows in the order you want
The keys appear on the row from left to right in the order of this list.
Arrow keys on top
Show the arrow keys row above the keys instead of under the spacebar
The row moves to the top of the keyboard, above the number row when that is on. It keeps the same keys, order and height.
Number row keys
Arrow keys row keys
Built-in row, for all layouts
Your own row, for all layouts that do not have their own

All layouts that do not have their own number row show this row, in all your languages. It shows above the letters, the symbols and the Fn layer. The second symbols page keeps its own row. A row that you set in a layout\'s editor comes first. Press a key to change it. Press and hold a key, then drag, to move it.

All layouts that do not have their own arrow keys row show this row, in all your languages. A row that you set in a layout\'s editor comes first. You can add any key, such as Word left or a second Shift. Press a key to change it. Press and hold a key, then drag, to move it.
Keys
Use the built-in row
Remove your changes from this row
The row as a list of keys, in the format that layouts use
Number row JSON
Arrow keys row JSON
Left
Up

Symbols layer
Go back to the letters
Leave ?123 after you type one of these characters

You change to ?123 for one full stop or one question mark, and the keyboard changes back to the letters after it. Turn this off to stay on the symbols layer until you press ABC. The emoji panel has the same setting.
Characters that go back
Go back after a space
Leave ?123 when you press the spacebar

You type a number or a symbol on ?123, press space, and the keyboard changes back to the letters for the next word. Turn this off to stay on the symbols layer, for example to type a phone number with spaces in it. This works on its own, with or without Go back to the letters.

Type the characters that send the keyboard back to the letters. Spaces between them are optional. An empty box uses the default characters ! ? . , ; and :. Digits are not in the default set, because you usually type more than one digit at a time.
Numerals
Type native digits in
Where the keyboard types the native digits
Number, phone, date and time fields keep 0-9, so they stay machine-readable
Native digits in those fields too
The keys show the glyphs, but they always type 0-9

You select the digit glyphs for each language under Languages → the language → Numerals. This setting controls where the keyboard also types those glyphs. \"Text fields\" is the default. It types 0-9 in number, phone, date and time fields, which keeps them machine-readable. In all other fields it types the native digits. \"Everywhere\" types the native digits in those fields too. \"Display only\" shows the glyphs on the keys but always types 0-9.
You set the digits for each language under Languages. The digits are Latin 0-9, Arabic ٠-٩, Persian ۰-۹, Bengali ০-৯ and Devanagari ०-९.
Size and position
Key height and keyboard size
Resize by dragging
Opens the keyboard with handles on its edges: drag the height, position and side margins in place
Resize
Key height
The height of each key row, which sets the total keyboard height
Tall keys are easier to press, but the keyboard covers more of the screen. The emoji, clipboard and snippet panels change size with this value too.
Bottom row height
The height of the space and enter row on its own

The bottom row holds the spacebar and enter. Give it a height that is taller or shorter than the letter keys, to get a larger spacebar without a taller keyboard. \"Follow keys\" is the default and keeps the bottom row the same height as the other rows. Custom layouts that set their own row heights ignore this setting.
Follow keys
Left padding
Move the left edge of the keyboard toward the centre

The keyboard keeps this much of the screen width clear on the left. The keys move toward the middle for thumb reach, and the keyboard does not dock to one edge as one-handed mode does. The default is 0 percent. This setting applies on top of the keyboard width above.
Right padding
Move the right edge of the keyboard toward the centre

The keyboard keeps this much of the screen width clear on the right. Set it to the same value as the left padding for an even margin, or to a different one to shift the keys toward the hand you type with. The default is 0 percent.
Key spacing
The gap between the keys

This changes the space around each key. A larger value moves the keys apart and makes the keyboard a little taller, because the gap is part of each row. A smaller value moves the keys closer together. The default is 100 percent.
Extend edge keys into the gaps
A tap in the blank space at the end of a short row, or below the bottom row, types the nearest key

Some rows are shorter than the keyboard, for example the A to L row of QWERTY. They have blank space at the left and right ends. With this setting on, a tap in that space types the key at that end of the row, so a tap to the left of A types A. Also, a tap in the space below the bottom row types the key above it, so a tap below the space bar types a space. The keys do not change size or position. Only the area that you can tap gets larger. This setting is off by default.
Bottom padding
More space below the keys, above the navigation bar
Full-height keyboard window
Changes of keyboard height redraw without a flicker. Turn off if the keyboard jumps when it hides

The keyboard\'s window covers the whole screen, with the keys at its bottom and the rest see-through, so a taller or shorter keyboard (selection mode\'s row, a panel\'s height bar, a tool opening) redraws in place instead of resizing the window, which on some phones showed a stale frame or the app\'s own toolbar for a moment.\n\nSome phones animate that whole window when the keyboard hides, so the keys jump up, stop halfway down and then vanish. Turn this off there and the window is as tall as the keyboard again. Off by default on Huawei phones.
Hide the system keyboard bar
Remove the bar with the hide and switch keyboard buttons below the keys
Needs Android 16 or later
Not available with this navigation. Needs gesture navigation, and this phone may draw the bar itself

With gesture navigation, Android puts a bar below the keyboard. It has a button that hides the keyboard and a button that changes to a different keyboard. With this setting on, the keyboard asks Android to remove that bar. When the bar is gone, the keys move down into its space. If the keys still sit higher than you want, make Bottom padding smaller. To hide the keyboard, use Back. To change to a different keyboard, use the 🌐 key. Only Android 16 and later lets a keyboard remove the bar. On older versions, this setting is not available. With three-button navigation, or on phones that draw the bar as part of the system navigation bar, no keyboard can remove it, so the setting is not available there either. This setting is off by default.

The whole keyboard moves up, away from the bottom edge and the gesture navigation bar. Increase it if the bottom row is too near the edge of the screen, or if you start the system navigation by mistake.
Round top corners
Cut round corners into the top of the keyboard
Round bottom corners
Cut round corners into the bottom of the keyboard

The corners are cut out of the whole keyboard, and the app shows through them. Set the top and the bottom separately, and choose the corners under Which corners. Round bottom corners suit gesture navigation and a phone with round screen corners. This does not change the floating keyboard, which has round corners of its own. Both are square by default.
Square
Which corners
The corners that the two settings above make round
Keyboard width
Make the keyboard narrower

Below 100 percent the keyboard does not fill the whole screen. Select the edge that it sits at below. This helps on very wide screens. One-handed mode below is a quick preset, and it replaces this value while it is on.
Full-width toolbar
Keep the toolbar and suggestions across the whole screen while only the keys get narrower

With this on, the keyboard width and the left and right padding narrow only the key rows. The toolbar, the suggestion strip and the open panels still fill the whole width of the screen, like Samsung Keyboard on a tablet. It changes nothing while the keys already fill the screen. You can set it for each screen shape below, for example only for a tablet held sideways.
Toolbar height
The height of the toolbar and suggestion row above the keys

Set how tall the row of tools and suggestions above the keys is. A lower row leaves more room for the app, and a taller one makes the tools easier to press. On a phone held sideways the keyboard uses 70 percent of this height, unless you set a height for landscape below.
Keyboard position
Where the narrow keyboard sits: at the left edge, in the centre, or at the right edge.
Left
Centre
Right
Per-screen sizing

The sizes above are the sizes for a portrait (folded) screen. A landscape or unfolded screen can replace any of them, or scale the whole keyboard at one time. This helps on a foldable device, where the large inner screen often needs a smaller keyboard than the cover screen. Each value that you do not change follows portrait.
Follows portrait

Font size

When off, the keyboard stays full width here, even with one-handed mode on

When off, the keyboard stays in one piece here, even with split keyboard on

One-handed, split and floating
One-handed, split, floating
One-handed mode
Make the keyboard smaller at one edge of the screen
You can set one-handed mode for each orientation. In the keyboard, the arrow on the rail changes the side and saves it here for that orientation.
Layout in one-handed mode
The layout to use while one-handed mode is on

Use a different layout of the same language while the keyboard is one-handed, such as QWERTY one-handed and One-row QWERTY otherwise. Turn one-handed mode off and the keyboard goes back to the layout you normally type on.\n\nThe list only shows enabled layouts that share a language with another enabled layout, since the choice applies only while you type in its language. In any other language, the keyboard keeps its normal layout. A layout set by a Keyboard Mode still comes first. The default is Same as normal.
Same as normal
Enable two layouts of one language to pick one here
Portrait only
Use the whole width when the phone is sideways

One-handed mode is one setting for both orientations, so a keyboard made small for a thumb in portrait stays small after you turn the phone, where you may want a split keyboard instead. Turn this on to keep one-handed mode in portrait and switch it off in landscape. Turn the phone back and it comes back. This setting is off by default.
Portrait
Landscape
%1$s width
How wide the keyboard is in %1$s
This is the part of the screen width that the keyboard uses while one-handed mode is on. The rail and empty space fill the rest, toward the centre.
%1$s height
Make the keys shorter for easier reach
This changes the key height while one-handed mode is on, and it brings the top rows down into thumb reach. 100 percent keeps the normal height.
%1$s side
The edge that the keyboard docks to in %1$s
Split keyboard
Divide the keys into a left half and a right half

The keyboard divides each row in the middle and puts a gap between the halves, so your thumbs move less on wide screens. This helps most on tablets, foldable devices and phones in landscape. By default the keyboard also divides the spacebar between the two halves.
Split gap
The width of the gap between the halves
This is the gap in the centre, as a percentage of the keyboard width. A larger gap moves the halves toward the edges, but each key becomes narrower.
Floating keyboard
Put the keyboard in a panel that you can move while the phone is upright

The keyboard becomes a small panel that floats above the apps, and it does not dock to the bottom of the screen. Drag the pill on the panel\'s handle bar to move it. Drag the corner grip to change the size. Press the dock button to go back to the normal keyboard. Apps do not change size while the panel floats, and touches outside the panel go to the app. Portrait and landscape each remember their own choice, so the floating tool and the dock button only change the one the phone is held in.
Floating in landscape
Float the keyboard while the phone is sideways
Full-screen typing in landscape
Type into a text box that covers the app
Full-screen typing upright
Use the same text box with the phone upright

Android only uses the large text box with a Done button when the phone is sideways. Turn this on to type into it with the phone upright too, which shows what you write in big, plain text away from the app. Floating, handwriting and tablets never use it. This setting is off by default.

When you hold the phone sideways, Android normally replaces the app with a large text box and a Done button while you type, because the keyboard leaves little room. Turn this off to keep the app in view above the keyboard, as in portrait. Some apps turn the text box off on their own. Tablets and unfolded phones never use it. This setting is on by default.

Turn this on and off on its own to float the keyboard sideways and keep it docked upright, or the other way round. The keyboard changes as soon as you turn the phone. Until you change one of the two, landscape follows the portrait switch.
Handle bar position
Where the floating panel\'s drag bar and resize grip sit

The handle bar holds the dock button, the drag pill and the resize grip. Under the keys is the default, where your thumb already is. With the bar under the keys, drag the grip down to make the panel taller. With the bar above the keys, drag it up.
Under the keys
Above the keys
Floating keyboard width
You can also drag the corner grip of the panel
This is the width of the floating panel. The key heights still follow the sliders above.
Keep the keyboard on screen
Stay open when no text field has focus
Allow display over other apps
The button cannot appear until Android allows it

After the keyboard opens, it stays on screen when the text field closes, and over apps that have no text field. This lets you send keys and keyboard shortcuts to an app, for example to set a hotkey in a notes app. To close the keyboard, press the hide key, swipe down on the toolbar, or press Back. It opens again the next time you tap a text field. The keyboard never stays on the lock screen. Works docked or floating.
Bottom row keys
Comma key opens emoji
Replace the comma key with an emoji key
Symbols page
The page the ?123 key opens
Standard
Number pad

Standard puts a row of digits over two rows of symbols. Number pad puts the digits on the right like a phone keypad, with the common symbols in narrow columns beside them, the way SwiftKey arranges its symbols page. On the number pad page, the {&= key opens the second symbols page. A layout that has its own symbols page keeps it. The number row and the 1234 key do not appear over the number pad page, because it already has every digit.
1234 key on the symbol pages
A key after ABC that opens the number pad

The symbol pages get a 1234 key directly after the ABC key, as in Gboard. Press it to open the number pad panel over the current field. The spacebar gets narrower by one key to make room. A layout that already has a number pad key, or a symbol page you arranged by hand in the layout editor, does not change.
Text editing key on the symbol pages
A key after ABC, or after 1234, that opens the text editing panel

The symbol pages get a key that opens the text editing panel: arrows, select, copy, cut, paste, undo and redo. It sits after the 1234 key when that key is on, otherwise directly after the ABC key. The spacebar gets narrower by one key to make room. This setting is off by default, because a new key on the bottom row is easy to press by accident. A layout that already has a text editing key, or a symbol page you arranged by hand in the layout editor, does not change.

The comma key on the bottom row becomes an emoji key, and the comma moves into the press and hold alternates. This also deletes the emoji tool from the toolbar, because the key replaces it. Drag the tool out of the toolbox again if you want both.
Emoji key instead of 🌐
Replace the language key with an emoji key

The 🌐 key on the bottom row opens the emoji panel and does not change the language. You can still change the language from the spacebar. Set a swipe to \"Language\" under Typing → Gestures. A short swipe does this by default. Turn this off to get the 🌐 key back.
Bottom row
One bottom row for every layout

Draws the same bottom row on the letters page of every layout, instead of the row each layout comes with. The settings below still apply to it: the 🌐 key can be hidden, turned into the emoji key or swapped with the comma. Layouts with a bottom row of their own, such as 12-key pads and kana boards, keep it, and so does a layout whose bottom row you arranged by hand in the layout editor.
As laid out
Each layout keeps its own bottom row
Classic
\?123 · , · space · . · enter. Languages change on the spacebar
iPhone-like
\?123 · 🌐 · space · enter
Minimal
\?123 · space · enter. Punctuation is on the symbols page
With emoji
\?123 · emoji · , · 🌐 · space · . · enter. The 🌐 key stays a language key
Key with your hold actions
Its long press shows the actions below

The actions you add below go at the end of this key\'s long-press popup, after anything it already offers, on every layout. Enter keeps its line break first in fields that send or search. On the 🌐 key the popup takes the place of the language picker; holding the spacebar opens it unless you gave the spacebar characters to hold.
Enter
Comma
Hold actions
Added to that key\'s long-press popup
None
Add an action
No actions yet. Each one you add shows after what the key already offers.
Move up
Move down
Key in place of 🌐
What the key in the 🌐 key\'s place opens
Emoji
The emoji panel
Swap the comma and 🌐 keys
Put the comma next to the spacebar
Keep the 🌐 key in one place
The same place on every layout, beside the spacebar

Some layouts put the 🌐 key in a different place, for example at the far left, or directly after the ?123 key. This moves it to the place the built-in layouts use, so your thumb finds it in the same place in every language. The keys to its left get wider or narrower to make room, and the spacebar changes to fit. A layout where that would make keys too small is left as it is, and so is a second layout you open from a key. Turn this off to see every layout as its author made it.
The two keys on each side of the spacebar change places. If one of them is an emoji key, it moves to the outer position and the comma stays next to the spacebar. Turn this off to get the usual order.
Show the 🌐 key
Turn off to give its space to the spacebar

When this is off, the 🌐 key is not on the bottom row of any layout. If \"Emoji key instead of 🌐\" is on, the emoji key in that position goes too. The spacebar gets the space. You can still change the language from the spacebar. Set a swipe to \"Language\" under Typing → Gestures. A short swipe does this by default.
🌐 goes back to the last language
Tap quickly to go further back

When this is on, one tap on the 🌐 key goes back to the layout you used before this one, and the next tap comes back again. This is useful with many languages when you only type two or three of them at a time. Tap several times quickly to go further back, most recently used first. A list shows where you are. When this is off, each tap goes to the next layout in your switch order. This also changes the language key on a physical keyboard. This setting is off by default.
Ignore 🌐 right after typing
A tap on 🌐 just after a letter does nothing

The 🌐 key is next to the spacebar and the comma, so a fast thumb can hit it by mistake in the middle of a word and change the language. Set a time here and a tap on 🌐 that comes sooner than this after a typed key does nothing. A tap after a pause changes the language as usual, and so do quick taps one after the other on 🌐 itself. Press and hold 🌐 to open the language list at any time. Letters, space, backspace and enter count as typing. Shift and the mode keys do not. This setting is off by default.
Split only on wide screens
Stay whole on a portrait phone, split when there is room
Split the spacebar
Divide the spacebar too, or keep it as one key across the gap
See-through gap
Show the app between the halves, and let taps there reach it

When this is on, the gap between the two halves of a split keyboard is see-through: you see the app behind it, and a tap in the gap goes to the app, as it does above the keyboard. The toolbar, the suggestion strip and any open panel still take the whole width. A spacebar that is kept as one key across the gap stays solid. It works for the docked keyboard only, not the floating one. This setting is off by default.

When this is on, the spacebar is divided between the two halves like every other row, and the centre of the bottom row is empty. When this is off, the spacebar stays as one key and fills the gap, so both thumbs can press it where they meet. The other keys on the bottom row stay in their halves. This setting is on by default.

Split is one setting for every screen shape, so turning it on in landscape leaves the keyboard split after you rotate back, where a split layout is hard to use. Turn this on to split only in landscape or on an unfolded screen. This setting is off by default.
Floating keyboard height
How tall the floating panel is, as a share of the normal key height
The resize grip on the floating panel changes this by dragging. The slider is here so you can set an exact height, and undo a drag that went too far. This setting is 100% by default.
Reset the floating panel
Put it back to the middle at its starting size
Reset size and position
Put every slider in this group back to its default
Key height, number row height, bottom row height, padding, width, position, spacing and corner radius all go back to their defaults. Per screen shape settings are not affected.
